paragraphs.source_en: On the morning of the twenty-third day of the fifth month in the twentieth year of Keichō, Katagiri Katsumoto learned that Kunimatsumaru, Toyotomi Hideyori's orphaned son, had been captured and was to be executed on the riverbank at Rokujō. At the time he was staying at the home of Matsuda Shōemon in Sanjō Koromodana, Kyoto. He was already bedridden and coughed up blood every day. Fearing that his ailing body could not withstand the shock, Shōemon's wife told him the news with fear and trembling.
